message.content:
You are auditing the customer-portal shell/navigation of a VPS hosting platform at /opt/nxeon. READ EVERY LINE of these files (use Read, absolute paths). Do NOT edit anything — report only.

FILES (read all, every line):
- /opt/nxeon/components/portal/Shell.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/components/portal/CommandPalette.tsx

Context: this is the persistent chrome around every dashboard page — top bar, sidebar nav, mobile drawer, notifications dropdown, command palette (Cmd-K), user menu.

HUNT for these defects specifically:
1. MOBILE DRAWER a11y at 390px: Does pressing Escape close the drawer? Is there a close button? Does the hamburger button have an aria-label and aria-expanded? When closed, is the drawer removed from the tab order (aria-hidden / inert / not visible), or are its ~25 links still tabbable? Backdrop click to dismiss?
2. KEYBOARD FOCUS visibility: are focus-visible styles present on nav items, buttons, the palette?
3. COMMAND PALETTE: uncontrolled search input inside a `<form action={fn}>`? (Probably client useState — that's fine.) Does it trap focus, close on Escape, have an accessible name? Any dead navigation (links to routes that 404)?
4. NOTIFICATIONS dropdown: mark-as-read that reports success without doing it; empty state quality.
5. MOBILE horizontal overflow at 390px: any fixed widths, hardcoded left gutters (e.g. lg:left-60) that don't match a collapsed rail width, grid/flex children with long unbreakable strings lacking min-w-0.
6. UNCONTROLLED FORM INPUTS inside any `<form action={serverFn}>`.
7. DEAD ENDS: disabled controls without explanation, links to nowhere.

OUTPUT: (a) one-line verdict per file (CLEAN / DEFECT / concerns), confirming you read every line; (b) each defect: file:line, what a customer experiences, minimal fix, quoting the code line. Precise line numbers. Do not fix anything.

content.thinking: I'll start by reading both files to understand what we're working with.

I've read through both files and I'm now checking them against the accessibility defect list. Starting with the mobile drawer: the escape key properly closes it, there's a close button with appropriate aria-label, and the hamburger menu has aria-label and aria-expanded attributes set correctly.

The drawer is properly removed from tab order when hidden using the inert attribute and aria-hidden. The backdrop click to close works as expected. One thing I'm noticing though — when the drawer opens, focus isn't automatically moved into it, so keyboard and screen reader users stay focused on the hamburger button. That's a minor accessibility concern. Also, there's no focus trap implemented, though the escape key and close button do provide ways out.

Now I'm looking at keyboard focus visibility — checking whether the nav items and buttons have proper focus-visible styles defined in the CSS.  The command palette input has `outline-none` which removes the focus ring, but since it's the only focusable element when the palette is open and focus is managed through keyboard navigation via arrow keys, that's acceptable. The result buttons don't have focus-visible styling and rely on mouse-driven active states, which means keyboard navigation through them would be less visible. I can't fully verify the nav-item and btn-ghost focus styles from these files, so I'll flag that as unconfirmed.

For the command palette itself, there's no focus trap, which is a minor concern. It does close on escape, which is good.

The bigger accessibility issue: the input has only a placeholder for its accessible name, which is technically a fallback per ARIA spec but not ideal. More critically, the modal overlay has no `role="dialog"` or `aria-modal="true"` attributes, so screen readers won't announce it as a dialog. The palette also references `/api/search` for results, but I can't verify those routes from here.

Looking at the notifications dropdown, there's a real bug: when opening it, if there are unread notifications, it calls `markNotificationsRead()` in a transition. But the notifications prop comes from the server and doesn't update client-side, so the unread count and bold styling won't refresh until a page reload.

The UX is also questionable — it marks all notifications as read the moment you open the dropdown, before the user actually reads anything. The logic itself is correct (checking `!notifOpen` before toggling), but marking everything read on open rather than on actual view feels premature, though it's a common pattern. The empty state shows "All caught up" which is fine.

There's a bigger issue though: the notifications dropdown has no click-outside handler to close it. The command palette and mobile drawer have backdrops, but this dropdown stays open until you click a notification link or toggle the bell again. If you open it and click elsewhere on the page, it just hangs there. There's also no Escape key to close it. Additionally, notification links default to `href="#"` when there's no href, which just scrolls to the top of the page instead of doing anything useful.

On mobile at 390px, the layout seems mostly fine — the sidebar translates off-screen, the notifications dropdown fits at 320px width, and the search button shrinks appropriately with its max-width constraint. The notification content itself handles text wrapping correctly with proper flex constraints.

The logout form is straightforward with just a button, no uncontrolled inputs to worry about. But I'm spotting some accessibility gaps: the notifications bell button has no aria-label or title, so screen readers won't announce what it does — just "button" with maybe the unread count. The collapse toggle also lacks an aria-label, only has a title attribute. The search button at least has visible text for its accessible name, so that's fine.

The notifications dropdown is a bigger concern — it's not a proper menu or dialog, can't be dismissed with Escape (the Escape handler only closes the sidebar), and clicking outside doesn't close it either. You have to click the bell again or follow a link. The command palette has similar issues: no dialog role, no aria-modal, the input lacks a proper accessible name beyond the placeholder, and there's no focus trap.

So the concrete defects are: notifications bell has no accessible name, the dropdown can't be dismissed properly, a notification with a null href points to "#" as a dead end, and the command palette lacks proper dialog semantics and focus management. The mark-as-read action seems to fire on open, which might be unexpected behavior.

I need to verify whether the server action actually revalidates the path — if it doesn't, the unread badge could persist visually even after marking as read. The drawer itself looks solid with good accessibility handling, but there's a minor concern: when the drawer opens on mobile, focus isn't trapped inside it, so keyboard users could tab from the drawer back into the page content behind the backdrop.

Now I'm checking the palette for horizontal overflow — the truncate classes handle it properly. Let me map out the specific line numbers for each issue: the notifications bell has no aria-label (lines 532-547), the dropdown lacks click-away or escape handling (lines 548-581), there's a dead-end href fallback (line 560), and the palette dialog is missing semantic attributes like dialog role and aria-modal (lines 84-91), plus the input has no accessible name (lines 97-117).

I've reviewed all 614 lines of Shell.tsx and all 143 lines of CommandPalette.tsx. Shell has defects around the unlabeled notifications bell and non-dismissible dropdown, though the drawer accessibility is genuinely clean. CommandPalette has concerns with missing dialog semantics and focus management, but it's otherwise functional.

content.text:
I read every line of both files (Shell.tsx: all 614 lines; CommandPalette.tsx: all 143 lines). Full audit below.

## (a) Per-file verdict

- **/opt/nxeon/components/portal/Shell.tsx — DEFECT.** The mobile-drawer a11y the prompt worried about is genuinely CLEAN (Escape, close button, hamburger `aria-label`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`, `inert`+`aria-hidden` when closed, backdrop-dismiss are all present and correct). The real defects are in the **notifications** UI: the bell has no accessible name, and the dropdown can't be dismissed by click-away or Escape. One minor dead-end href.
- **/opt/nxeon/components/portal/CommandPalette.tsx — concerns.** Functionally solid (controlled `useState` input — not in any `<form action>`; Escape closes; ⌘K/Ctrl-K toggle; arrow/Enter nav; results truncate). But it's not a real dialog: no `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`, no focus trap, input's only accessible name is its placeholder, and focus isn't restored on close.

## (b) Defects

**1. Shell.tsx:532-538 — Notifications bell button has NO accessible name.** It's an icon-only button (SVG bell + unread-count span) with no `aria-label` and no `title`. A screen-reader customer hears only "button" (or "button, 3" from the count) with no idea it opens notifications. Contrast the sign-out button one block down (line 594) which correctly has `title="Sign out"`.
```
<button
  className="btn-ghost relative rounded-xl p-2.5"
```
Minimal fix: add `aria-label="Notifications"` (ideally reflecting unread count) to that `<button>`.

**2. Shell.tsx:548-581 — Notifications dropdown can't be dismissed by click-away or Escape.** The panel only closes by clicking the bell again (toggle) or clicking a notification link (line 561). Unlike the command palette and mobile drawer, it has no backdrop overlay and no key handler, so a customer who opens it and clicks anywhere else on the page is stuck with it floating open over their content. The Escape listener at lines 290-297 is gated on `sidebarOpen`, so Escape does nothing here either.
```
{notifOpen && (
  <div className="absolute right-0 top-12 z-30 w-80 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl ...">
```
Minimal fix: render an invisible full-screen click-away layer while `notifOpen` (as done for the palette/drawer), and/or add Escape-to-close.

**3. Shell.tsx:560 — Notification without an href is a dead end.** When `n.href` is null the row links to `"#"`, so clicking a hrefless notification jumps the page to the top / does nothing meaningful (and still fires `setNotifOpen(false)`, so it just closes with no navigation).
```
href={n.href ?? "#"}
```
Minimal fix: render hrefless notifications as a non-link `<div>` (or `<button>` that only closes), not an anchor to `"#"`.

**4. Shell.tsx:534-537 — Mark-as-read fires on open and the badge won't visibly clear.** Opening the bell immediately calls `markNotificationsRead()` before the customer reads anything, so all unread markers are consumed on open. More concretely, `unread` (line 305) and the bold/dot styling derive from the `notifications` **prop**; nothing updates it client-side, so unless the server action calls `revalidatePath`, the blue count badge and bold titles persist for the rest of the session even though they're now "read" server-side — a confusing mismatch.
```
setNotifOpen((v) => !v);
if (!notifOpen && unread > 0) startTransition(() => markNotificationsRead());
```
Minimal fix: optimistically clear unread locally (e.g. `useOptimistic`/local state) so the UI matches, and confirm the action revalidates. (The open-toggle logic itself is correct — `!notifOpen` reads the pre-toggle state, so it only fires on open.)

**5. CommandPalette.tsx:84-117 — palette isn't an accessible modal dialog.** The overlay/inner divs have no `role="dialog"` / `aria-modal="true"`, there's no focus trap (Tab can leave the input and land on page content behind the z-50 backdrop), and the input's only accessible name is its `placeholder` (line 100). `outline-none` at line 99 also strips the input's focus ring. Focus is set into the input on open (line 43) but never restored to the ⌘K trigger on close. None of this breaks mouse use, but keyboard/SR users get a leaky, unlabeled modal.
```
99  className="w-full bg-transparent text-sm outline-none placeholder:text-slate-500"
100  placeholder="Search servers, domains, tickets, pages…"
```
Minimal fix: add `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` + an `aria-label` on the outer panel, `aria-label="Search"` on the input, trap focus within the panel, and restore focus on close.

## Items checked and found CLEAN
- **Mobile drawer at 390px:** Escape closes (290-297), visible close button with `aria-label="Close menu"` (357-366), hamburger has `aria-label`/`aria-expanded`/`aria-controls` (490-496), closed drawer is `inert` + `aria-hidden` via `drawerHidden` so its ~25 links leave the tab order (285, 347-348), backdrop-click dismiss (463-465), route-change auto-close (301-303). This is a genuinely well-fixed drawer.
- **Uncontrolled inputs in `<form action={serverFn}>`:** none. The only such form is `<form action={logout}>` (593) and it contains only a button. The palette input is controlled `useState` and not inside any form.
- **Horizontal overflow at 390px:** main column has `min-w-0 flex-1` (468); sidebar footer email uses `truncate` (435); palette rows use `truncate`/`flex-1` (134-135); notification body uses `min-w-0 flex-1` (568). The old `lg:left-60` vs collapsed-rail mismatch is addressed via the `--nx-rail-w` variable (258-260).

## Couldn't verify from these two files
Focus-visible styling for `nav-item` and `btn-ghost` lives in external CSS (not in these files), so I can't confirm keyboard focus rings on the sidebar links/buttons. Whether notification/search routes 404 depends on `/api/search` and the server-provided `nav`/`notifications` data, which aren't in scope here.
